# Rs-online.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/rs-online-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/rs-online-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects product and listing data from Rs-online.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape RS-Online (rs-online.com) in 2026](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-rs-online)
- **Code:** [`rs_online.py`](rs_online.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Category](results/category.json) · [Products](results/products.json) · [Search](results/search.json)

## What it scrapes

- RS Online product pages for product data, pricing, stock, specifications and compliance info
- RS Online category pages for product listing data
- RS Online keyword search pages for product listing data

## Functions

- `scrape_products(urls)` → `List[RSProduct]`
- `scrape_category(url, max_pages=3)` → `List[RSSearchResult]`
- `scrape_search(query, max_pages=3)` → `List[RSSearchResult]`

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import rs_online


async def main():
    products = await rs_online.scrape_products(
        urls=[
            "https://us.rs-online.com/product/aim-cambridge-cinch-connectivity-solutions/40-9715m/70081087/",
            "https://us.rs-online.com/product/cinch/dah15s/70152743/",
        ],
    )
    category = await rs_online.scrape_category(
        url="https://us.rs-online.com/connectors/d-sub-connectors-contacts-accessories/d-sub-connectors/",
        max_pages=2,
    )
    search = await rs_online.scrape_search(query="transformer", max_pages=2)


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`RSProduct`**: `name`, `url`, `rs_stock_number`, `mpn?`, `brand?`, `description?`, `price?`, `currency?`, `availability?`, `stock_quantity?`, `min_order_qty?`, `qty_increment?`, `tiered_pricing?`, `lead_time_required?`, `datasheet_url?`, `image?`, `specifications`, `compliance`, `category?`
- **`RSSearchResult`**: `name?`, `url?`, `rs_stock_number?`, `mpn?`, `price?`, `currency?`, `availability?`, `stock_quantity?`, `image?`

A field marked `?` can be `null`.

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`rs_online.py`](rs_online.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `country` = `"us"`: country of the proxy
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)
- `rendering_wait` = `5000`: wait after the page rendered, in milliseconds

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/rs-online-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_product_scraping`, `test_category_scraping`, `test_search_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
